author: David Reed
summary: Closes the silent-fallback pattern iter-14 fixed one instance of. chg-19: GuidelineRetriever.query() returns a RetrievalOutcome instead of a str, covering guideline-retrieval fallback and a separate precedents-failure axis, so degradation is visible instead of only a log line. chg-20: the submit route always audits a degraded retrieval and, behind a PATCH-/config-tunable warn-default flag, can force human review with a persisted decision instead of reasoning over unverified fallback context.

changes.description: GuidelineRetriever.query() returns RetrievalOutcome(text, mode, degraded, reason, precedents_degraded, precedents_reason) instead of a bare str. mode is pipeline (intended path), direct_fallback (pipeline unavailable/raised, fallback found something), or empty (fallback found nothing). reason is the exception TYPE name only, never the raw message. precedents_degraded/precedents_reason track precedent retrieval failing during an otherwise-healthy pipeline call.
changes.failure_pattern: GuidelineRetriever.query() catches any exception from the real RAGPipeline, logs at error level, and silently falls back to the legacy direct-ChromaDB path, returning a plausible-looking str either way. The caller (the submit route, the DecisionAgent's prompt context) cannot distinguish governed retrieval from degraded retrieval. vector_store.py has the highest density of broad `except Exception` in the codebase (5 in 353 lines); this is the constructor/query pair that feeds a clinical decision.
changes.root_cause: The return type of query() was always `str`, so there was no channel for the method to say 'I degraded' short of a log line at error level — which nothing downstream reads. iter-14 (chg-17) fixed one concrete instance of this pattern (a bad import that latched the fallback permanently) but did not change the return type, so any future pipeline failure — a ChromaDB connection error, an embedding-function exception, a malformed query — reproduces the same invisible degradation.

evidence.note: "a silent fallback plus an unimportable module is indistinguishable from a working system" — the general claim this change acts on, not just the specific import bug iter-14 fixed.
Before this change there was no way to express or test 'the pipeline never ran and the fallback found nothing' as a distinct, non-crashing outcome — it looked identical to a healthy empty result.
Regression guard: a synthetic PHI-like exception message is asserted absent from RetrievalOutcome.reason — only the exception's type name crosses the boundary that chg-20 writes into an audit record.

Adversarial-Validator finding (HIGH, pre-merge): the first draft of this change surfaced guideline-retrieval degradation but left _query_precedents' own except-and-swallow untouched, so a total precedents outage on an otherwise-healthy pipeline call still reported mode='pipeline', degraded=False. Fixed by threading a (text, failure_reason) result out of _query_precedents into the new precedents_degraded/precedents_reason fields.

predicted_fixes: A RAGPipeline failure (ChromaDB error, embedding-function exception, any future exception in the retrieval path) is now distinguishable from a healthy retrieval by mode/degraded on the return value, not just a log line.

An unseeded or genuinely empty retrieval (mode='empty') is distinguishable from a real fallback that found something (mode='direct_fallback'), so an operator reading audit records can tell 'degraded but real context' from 'the agent decided on nothing'.
Every existing call site of query() (7 files found by repo-wide grep) is updated in the same change, per repo lesson P-005 on contract changes.

A precedents-collection-only failure during a healthy pipeline call now flips RetrievalOutcome.degraded to True via precedents_degraded, instead of being indistinguishable from 'no precedents matched'.
risk_cases: Any call site not caught by the grep for '.query(' would silently break (AttributeError on .text) rather than degrade gracefully — mitigated by grepping the whole repo, not just files already open.

A test double that still returns a bare str instead of a RetrievalOutcome would raise inside the route rather than being caught by the existing except Exception -> 500 handler in a semantically odd way — verified none remain by running the full non-clinical suite.
changes.why_this_component: The defect is in the retrieval tool's return contract, not in how any agent reasons over the text it receives — the agent-visible prompt content is unchanged in shape (still `.text`), only the caller's ability to detect degradation changed.
changes.rollback_plan: Revert all files in this change together (one commit per file, three commits: vector_store.py, the authorizations.py call-site fix, and the test call-site updates). A partial revert of just vector_store.py breaks every call site immediately (AttributeError on .text); revert the full set or not at all.

changes.description: The submit route audits every degraded RetrievalOutcome (action=rag.degraded, details cover both the guideline-mode axis and the precedents axis) before proceeding. A new settings.rag_degraded_escalates flag (default False, read via effective_settings, patchable through PATCH /config) can force human review (IN_REVIEW/HUMAN, EscalationReason.RAG_DEGRADED) instead of reasoning over unverified fallback context. The escalated decision is persisted so it is visible on GET /review-queue.
changes.failure_pattern: Even after chg-19 makes degradation visible in the return value, nothing acted on it: a degraded RetrievalOutcome could still flow straight into the DecisionAgent's prompt with no audit trail and no escalation path, leaving the same clinical-visibility gap one layer up the call stack.
changes.root_cause: Visibility (chg-19) and policy (chg-20) are different constraint levels — the return-type contract belongs in the tool implementation, but 'what happens when it's degraded' is a governance/escalation decision that belongs at the route, alongside the existing ScopeViolation and evidence-grounding short-circuits.

evidence.note: Direct precedent for the warn-then-enforce rollout shape reused here: land audited-but-non-blocking, promote once production degradation rates are known.

Drives the real submit_authorization handler with a degraded RetrievalOutcome and rag_degraded_escalates=True (flipped via apply_overrides, the same runtime path PATCH /config uses); asserts IN_REVIEW/HUMAN, the escalation audit record, that the orchestrator never runs, AND that DecisionRepository.create persists the escalated decision (see the two Validator findings below).
Adversarial-Validator-requested guard: rag_degraded_escalates=True with a healthy RetrievalOutcome must produce zero rag.degraded / escalation records — the predicate does not fire on the happy path.

First draft read this flag via get_settings() (the cached, process-start snapshot) and did not expose it on ConfigPatchRequest, so 'operators can flip it without another code change' was only true in the env-var-plus-restart sense. Fixed: the route now reads effective_settings(), and admin.py's ConfigPatchRequest gained the field (one line, src/pacca/api/routes/admin.py) so PATCH /config actually works.

First draft's enforce-mode escalation path returned AuthorizationDecision(status=IN_REVIEW) without calling DecisionRepository.create — GET /review-queue reads persisted IN_REVIEW rows, so the escalated case would never have appeared there: a human review nobody could see. Fixed by persisting before return, mirroring the normal-flow decision write further down this function. NOTE: the pre-existing ScopeViolation handler (same file, ~line 460) has the identical non-persistence defect (confirmed by the Validator) and was deliberately NOT touched here — it is shipped behavior from chg-9/iter-9 and needs its own manifest entry and falsifiable prediction in a future iteration, not a scope-creep fix bundled into chg-20.

The new escalation persist added above was itself the only ungoverned db.write_decision-class call site: the normal-flow persist is preceded by enforce_scope(intent, 'db.write_decision', ...), the escalation persist was not. Practical exposure was near zero (the write uses request.request_id, the exact value the guard checks), but the P-4 guard's value is the invariant that every governed write is wrapped. Fixed by adding the identical enforce_scope call before the escalation persist, same shape/mode as the existing one -- this is now the guard's third db.write_decision-class site (CLAUDE.md's component inventory updated to match, four sites total).

Both docstrings pre-dated the precedents_degraded axis and still described degradation as only 'the pipeline was unavailable or raised, and retrieval fell back' -- code-contradicts-doc per CLAUDE.md's doc-drift rule. Both updated to describe the two independent axes (guideline-mode fallback vs. precedents-only failure with no fallback).

predicted_fixes: Every RAG degradation in production now leaves an audit record (action='rag.degraded') regardless of the escalation flag, closing the 'no trace of what context the agent actually saw' gap. The audit details also carry the precedents axis (precedents_degraded/precedents_reason), so a reader can tell which axis of retrieval failed.
Operators can flip rag_degraded_escalates to True at runtime via PATCH /admin/config (ConfigPatchRequest), once they have data on how often degradation fires, with no env change or process restart.
An escalated RAG-degraded case is persisted and therefore visible on GET /review-queue, not silently dropped.
The RAG-degraded escalation persist is now scope-guarded like every other db.write_decision call, so a future refactor of this block inherits the P-4 invariant instead of quietly bypassing it.
risk_cases: If degradation fires far more often than expected (e.g. a flaky embedding function), warn mode means many decisions proceed on fallback context before anyone notices — mitigated by the audit record being written every time, so the rate is observable without needing enforce mode on.

Flipping rag_degraded_escalates to True without first observing production rates could flood the human review queue, per the same risk the P-4 scope guard rollout was designed against — this is why the default stays False here.

The pre-existing ScopeViolation escalation path (same file) shares the non-persistence defect this change fixed for its own path; it was not fixed here (out of scope per the Validator's explicit instruction) and remains a known gap until it gets its own iteration.
changes.why_this_component: This is a new deterministic pre-agent short-circuit in the 7-branch escalation tree's spirit (though it lives in the route rather than the orchestrator, matching where the RAG query itself happens, before DecisionContext is built) — the same constraint level as SCOPE_VIOLATION, not a tool or prompt change.
changes.rollback_plan: Revert settings.py, enums.py, authorizations.py, and admin.py together (each landed as its own commit). Reverting only settings.py would leave a dangling EscalationReason.RAG_DEGRADED reference in authorizations.py; reverting admin.py alone would leave a PATCH /config field with no backing setting. Revert the full set or not at all.
